doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: The Vanguard albums and multiple takes
summary: Ware discusses the second Vanguard album and the modern issue of alternate takes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, he has said that that was an historic album in the sense that I guess, without the piano being able to do the things and that he could do, he said he could do it with a good bass player, and that is important. And then as we reach the other ... More from at the Vanguard, that was recorded at that same time.

That was recorded that night. The first group of tunes was in the afternoon, and that More from the Vanguard was later on that night, when everybody was retiring, and you know, and I guess he had to pick whether he wanted to put out, you know, the editing, and he just put these out, and it was a year ago? Or something like that ... a couple years ago.

But still some people like it. That's what is happening now. A whole lot of these recording companies they have, the thing where they make one master, two masters, and they put them out, you know; you approve one master and that's it. So of late, they been bringing out two or three different takes of the same tune.
